target_customer: Self-insured employers, third-party administrators and health plans that pay medical claims
problem: Self-insured payers overpay on claims because manual audits cover only high-dollar claims and TPAs are paid to process claims, not police them.
business_model: Contingency fee on realized savings with zero implementation fee

founders.name: Angel Onuoha
previous_startups: Zuvy (Lagos fintech, majority stake acquired by BAS Group in 2025)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a 3x founder who had three knee surgeries and was billed over $250K.

founders.name: Ahmad Shehu
previous_startups: Zuvy (Lagos fintech, majority stake acquired by BAS Group in 2025)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built healthcare data platforms for the Nigerian government serving over 20M people.

technical_complexity.rationale: Claim auditing models need coding, billing and contract knowledge plus clinician review and HIPAA-grade handling, which is standard ML engineering with domain hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Claims data from customers can compound model accuracy, but entrants can copy the contingency model and incumbents run rule engines.

incumbents: Claims auditing and cost containment vendors
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found as of late 2026 in the sources opened.

market_need_then: The YC page says self-insured employers waste over $60B a year on claims that should not have been paid; this figure is the company's own claim.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and punchy, short declarative headlines such as Recovery on autopilot.

brand_strength.rationale: Invented name with a health suffix that resembles Avalere and Avenir; no press about the brand was found.

pivots.from: Consumer AI agent that helped patients dispute medical bills
pivots.to: Payment integrity models that audit claims for self-insured employers and health plans
pivots.why: Per the YC page, the founders moved upstream to stop bad payments before patients see a bill after helping sixty patients cut over $300K of bills.

outcome_analysis: Avelis Health is early and active. The founders sold a prior fintech (Zuvy) in 2025 and moved from a consumer bill dispute agent to B2B claim auditing sold on contingency. Funding beyond the YC deal is thin: one outlet reports a round with Tekedia Capital in November 2025 with no amount. It is too early to call an outcome.
notes: Aggregators claim a $500K pre-seed from Y Combinator and list GFT Ventures and Rebel Fund as investors; these are unverified and the YC standard deal is not recorded as a round. A directory mentions a larger later round and PitchBook shows a deal in September 2025, both unverified. Zuvy buyer differs by source (BAS Group per founder profile and Finrate, a private equity firm per launch post). No dated competitor sources were found in the search, so the competitor list is empty.
